title: What happens to your brain when you study until 2 AM

lines.vo: At 2 AM, Leo read the same page for the ninth time, and remembered none of it.
lines.shot: Leo at his desk under the lamp, eyes drooping, flips back a page

lines.vo: Exam at nine. His plan: skip sleep, cram everything.
lines.shot: wall clock 2:00, stack of books, highlighter

lines.vo: Dude. You've highlighted the whole book.
Sleep is for people who already know this.
Three coffees later, he felt unstoppable.
Then, at nine: question one. Total blank.
lines.shot: exam room, Leo stares at the paper, dolly zoom

lines.vo: Here's what was happening inside his brain.
While you're awake, a chemical called adenosine piles up. That's what makes you sleepy.
lines.shot: brain panel filling with dots, Leo yawns

lines.vo: Coffee doesn't clear it. It just blocks the sensors, until it wears off and the crash hits.
lines.shot: coffee blocks the receptors; Leo's head drops

lines.vo: Up since 7 AM? By 2 AM that's 19 hours awake, and your brain performs like it's had a couple of drinks.
lines.shot: clock spin, card 19 h awake = 0.05% BAC

lines.vo: And your hippocampus holds the day's facts like a USB stick. Deep sleep copies them to the hard drive.
No sleep, no copy. And a full stick can't save anything new.
lines.shot: files bounce off the full stick

lines.vo: Leo found that out the hard way, because
